question: How do moths migrating high above Britain at night keep the wind that carries them from blowing them off course?
answer: They choose their night, height and heading. Radar studies by Chapman and colleagues found silver Y moths leaving in autumn mostly on northerly winds, climbing to where those winds blew fastest, and angling their bodies against any crosswind. They covered several hundred kilometres a night, far more than their own flight allows.
move: To ride a current well, choose when to board, where, and which way to face.
reference: Chapman et al., Flight orientation behaviors promote optimal migration trajectories in high-flying insects, Science, 2010
